sources.title: NOAA/NCEI: June 2026 global climate analysis
sources.publisher: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
sources.summary: NOAA/NCEI reported that June 2026 was the second-warmest June on record globally, with global ocean surface temperature the warmest on record for June, both poles ranking among their 10 lowest June sea ice extents, and above-average tropical cyclone activity.

sources.title: WMO: Global Seasonal Climate Update for August-September-October 2026
sources.summary: WMO's August-October 2026 update said a strong El Nino is developing and expected to strengthen, above-normal temperatures are expected worldwide, rainfall patterns show an El Nino footprint, and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole is expected to develop.

sources.title: Copernicus: Daily global sea surface temperatures break records for the time of year
sources.publisher: Copernicus Climate Change Service and Copernicus Marine Service
sources.summary: Copernicus reported that daily global sea surface temperatures exceeded previous record levels for the time of year, with C3S daily SST reaching 20.86 C on 21 June 2026 and Copernicus Marine indicating 21.0 C.

sources.title: NASA GISS: GISTEMP v4 dataset and monthly update schedule
sources.publisher: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies
sources.summary: NASA GISS describes GISTEMP v4 as a global surface temperature analysis updated about the 10th of each month using NOAA GHCN v4 station data and ERSST ocean data, providing a cross-checkable official dataset for temperature monitoring.
